title: RANSAC Scoring Done Right
claim: Threshold-based scores degrade sharply under hyperparameter miscalibration, while our scores stay flat across a two-decade range.
layout: 3 panels side by side, shared log x-axis, shared bottom legend
description: Three line-plot panels sit side by side. Each is titled with a dataset, feature type and geometric problem: PhotoTourism/RootSIFT/E, ETH3D/SuperPoint+LightGlue/F, and HEB/SIFT/H. The y-axis is median rotation error in degrees. The x-axis is the hyperparameter κ/κ*, on a log scale from 1/10 to 10. Solid colored curves show baselines (RANSAC, MSAC, GaU, MAGSAC++) and the proposed variants (Jeffreys, IG-Robust, IG-MLE), with shaded bootstrap confidence bands. Baseline curves form U shapes that rise steeply at the edges. In the first two panels the proposed curves are almost flat. Dashed horizontal lines in matching colors mark per-pair oracle tuning, and a thick black line marks the oracle. Filled dots mark each curve's minimum. In the third panel IG-Robust (green) stays low over most of the range. A shared legend runs along the bottom.
caption: Profile across three datasets, one per geometric problem: PT / $\bE$ (left), \ethd / $\bF$ (middle), \heb / $\bH$ (right). Each panel plots, as solid lines, the median rotation error across all pairs in the dataset versus each method's hyperparameter on a log axis, swept exhaustively over a two-decade interval. Color-matched dashed horizontal lines mark each method's achievable performance when its hyperparameter is free to be tuned per pair to select the model closest to the ground truth; a large gap to the solid curve indicates hyperparameter-dependent model switching. Filled circles mark each method's minimum on the fine grid; the axis is normalized by the coarse-search optimum, so $x = 1$ need not be a minimum. Shaded bands are 95% bootstrap confidence intervals on the median. In the data-rich regime (PT, \ethd) our variants are remarkably robust to hyperparameter miscalibration, with curves nearly flat across the full two-decade window where threshold-based baselines degrade markedly. On \heb---the data-scarce regime---the \igrobust prior regularizes the score and outperforms the baselines over most of the hyperparameter interval (cf. [ref]).
abstract: The most widely used RANSAC variants score a candidate model by summing per-point scores that fall to zero beyond a threshold. These scores derive from the negative log-likelihood of a Gaussian-uniform mixture. The threshold separates inliers, which follow the noise model, from outliers, and it is a function of the observation noise level, also known as the inlier scale. We remove this dependence on the threshold by reversing the usual order of RANSAC inference: rather than estimating the scale and then scoring against it, we marginalize the scale in closed form for a fixed inlier partition and then optimize over partitions. The resulting score is maximized by a single sort followed by a linear sweep. A single closed-form expression spans informative and non-informative priors, so the same score adapts to datasets with extensive or limited ground-truth annotation. The proposed score has a single hyperparameter, the half-width of the uniform outlier distribution. We show that this half-width is far less sensitive to miscalibration than the inlier threshold and is easier to cross-validate. The proposed score is the first likelihood-based RANSAC score in which the inlier scale is absent from the formula. Project page: https://ransacscoringdoneright.github.io
